questions.title: Rao-Blackwell risk decomposition and a Poisson conditioning example
questions.description: Focused known-result theory evaluation grounded in David Blackwell, Conditional Expectation and Unbiased Sequential Estimation, The Annals of Mathematical Statistics 18(1), 1947, pages 105-110, DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177730497, and C. R. Rao, Information and Accuracy Attainable in the Estimation of Statistical Parameters, Bulletin of the Calcutta Mathematical Society 37(3), 1945, pages 81-91. In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX theory workspace, let U be a square-integrable estimator of g(theta), let T be sufficient, and define delta(T)=E_theta[U given T] using a conditional law that is independent of theta. Derive rather than merely quote the exact squared-error decomposition E_theta[(U-g(theta))^2]=E_theta[(delta(T)-g(theta))^2]+E_theta[(U-delta(T))^2]. Establish the vanishing cross term through conditional expectation, state the integrability and parameter-version requirements, derive unbiasedness and the law-of-total-variance form, and characterize equality and strict improvement without claiming pointwise or uniform strictness. Then take n>=2 iid Poisson(lambda) observations, U=X_1, and S=sum_i X_i. Derive sufficiency of S by factorization, derive the full conditional mass function X_1 given S=s as Binomial(s,1/n) rather than naming a splitting fact, obtain delta(S)=S/n, and calculate its expectation, variance, squared-error risk, and exact improvement relative to X_1. Handle lambda=0 and n=1 honestly, explain why the conditional law is parameter-free, and distinguish Rao-Blackwell variance reduction from an unproved UMVU or completeness claim. Keep active and rejected calculations visibly distinct and disclose unresolved measure-theoretic or boundary gaps. This L0 task evaluates mathematical derivation and independent review only. Source replication, Python/R implementation, simulation, Lean formalization, and novelty claims are not applicable.
